headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network capabilities make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads files from the filesystem and OpenHands shares state via mounted volume/files in the runtime, so one agent can feed attacker-controlled content into the other through shared files. Mentat’s diff-based edits and OpenHands’ agent loop both consume file content, making instruction hijack plausible without extra isolation.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or mounted volume, injected instructions can cross from one to the other.
IF either agent treats file contents as trusted task context, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Disable shared mounted volumes between runtimes.
Review file contents before passing them between agents.
Prefix all inter-agent files as untrusted data.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code in selected files and OpenHands touches files mounted into its runtime; both have broad network egress and model-provider API usage, so sensitive code can flow into inference backends if the same workspace is shared. The pair’s default file-sharing path makes leakage plausible even without special configuration.
conditions: IF the same sensitive files are mounted into both runtimes, both agents can access them.
IF either agent sends file contents to its model backend, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Mount only minimal files needed for each agent.
Keep secrets out of shared workspaces.
Use local-only model backends where possible.
Rotate API keys after any sensitive-file session.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state, and Mentat explicitly shares state via filesystem while OpenHands shares state via mounted volume. Concurrent edits to the same repo can overwrite each other or corrupt git state, and no locking mechanism is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent commits or diffs can conflict.
IF both agents write the same files without external locking, one agent can clobber the other’s changes.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Serialize write access with a manual lock.
Have only one agent modify git state at a time.
Review and merge diffs before applying them.
requires-engineering: add repository-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals and OpenHands runs an agent loop with shell/browser/editor actions, so OpenHands can treat Mentat’s output as authoritative and then execute it. That creates a direct path from one agent’s mistaken or malicious edits to downstream actions, with potentially irreversible effects.
conditions: IF OpenHands consumes Mentat-generated diffs or instructions without verification, errors cascade into executed actions.
IF Mentat’s proposed edits contain incorrect facts, OpenHands may operationalize them.
mitigations: Require human review before execution.
Compare proposed diffs against source files.
Run OpenHands in read-only mode for the first pass.
Use a second verifier agent before applying changes.
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding agents with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. The main compliance concern is generic handling of source code and API keys, but the profiles do not show a specific cross-border or regulated-data violation pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into either workspace, compliance obligations may apply.
IF the operator routes sensitive code or secrets through third-party model APIs, retention policy review is required.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either workspace.
Use non-sensitive test repositories.
Review model-provider retention settings.
Store secrets outside shared folders.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
